provision.quote: Challenge is to show cause notice dated 18/06/2025 issued by respondent no.3, under Section 74 of The Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (for short “CGST Act”).

financial_years.quote: The notice dated 18/06/2025 pertains to financial years 2018-19 to 2022-23 saying that the petitioner has, during this period, suppressed taxable value, and thereby made short payments of Central Goods and Service Tax.

document_contents.quote: The notice dated 18/06/2025 pertains to financial years 2018-19 to 2022-23 saying that the petitioner has, during this period, suppressed taxable value, and thereby made short payments of Central Goods and Service Tax.

defects_argued.quote: There is no distinction made under Section 74 of the CGST Act that would permit the respondents to issue consolidated notices in a case where fraudulent availment of Input Tax Credits is alleged.

outcome.quote: With the above liberty, and for the reasons set out in Milroc Good Earth Developers (supra) and Rite Water Solutions (India) Ltd. (supra), the petition is partly allowed.
